card.name: Linking words after an opening clause
card.fires_on: Small linking words or verbs that follow a long introductory phrase and come just before the main statement, such as which, showed, when, that, of, the and a comma. Seen in news, science and drug-label sentences.

modes.label: Relative or reporting word
modes.description: A word like which, that, showed or reported that opens the clause carrying the main point.
modes.example: Despite recent drought, the study<< showed>> that the numbers of rare and endangered birds

modes.label: Comma after a long lead-in
modes.description: A comma ends a long introductory phrase, just before the main subject.
modes.example: umably because angiotensin-converting enzyme inhibitors affect the metabolism of eicosanoids and polypeptides, including endogenous bradykinin<<,>> patients receiving ACE inhibitors, including moex

modes.label: Plain connector
modes.description: A short connector such as when, the or of in the middle of a sentence, with the sentence still unfinished.
modes.example: Morris Frank & Buddy made history in 1928<< when>> they arrived in New York City as the

card.writes: It favors spacing and line-break characters over ellipsis marks, which suggests it does not push toward trailing off.
card.plain: It fires on little connecting words in the middle of a sentence, where the main point is still to come.
